articles.title: Rob Reiner’s son Jake gives first interview after parents’ deaths: ‘I will never understand why this happened’
articles.summary: Jake says his parents ‘never stopped helping’ his brother Nick, who has pleaded not guilty to murdering both of them at their Los Angeles home. Jake Reiner has given his first interview since the killing of his parents, the film-maker Rob Reiner and his wife, Michele Singer Reiner, saying: “I will…
body: Reiner, who directed films including The Princess Bride, This Is Spinal Tap and Stand By Me, was found dead alongside Singer Reiner from apparent stab wounds in their home in Los Angeles in December.
Their 32-year-old son, Nick Reiner, was indicted for two counts of first-degree murder and has pleaded not guilty.
If he is convicted, he could face the death penalty. Prosecutors have not yet indicated whether they will pursue capital punishment.
Jake and Nick’s sister, Romy Reiner, 28, lived across the street from her parents, and discovered the body of her father.

articles.title: ‘I don’t care if I look good’: French heartthrob Louis Garrel on fashion, fatherhood and his radically dorky new role
articles.summary: The star has long been French cinema’s favourite tousle-haired Adonis, which makes his latest performance – as a schlubby, stay-at-home dad – all the more surprising. ‘I appreciate people laughing at me,’ he says.
body: ‘E ven though I’ve been working in film for over 20 years, I still have this desire to look beautiful on screen,” says Louis Garrel, on a video call from his bed inside a boat off the coast of Corsica. The French film star is lying on his stomach, occasionally kicking up his bare legs, ruffling his curls and running the nail of his thumb over his moustache. I think the person he sees on the laptop screen in front of him is me, but I am pretty certain he is flirting with his own reflection.

The attraction between the Paris-born 43-year-old and the camera tends to be reciprocal. Long of limb, tousled of hair and chiselled of nose, Garrel has spent a career on screen as French cinema’s favourite Adonis – the man film-makers turn to when they need an erotic wrecking ball to smash up bourgeois twosomes and turn them into quivering menages a trois.

articles.summary: Vuelta’s sales and finance outfit Global Constellation has boarded international sales on “Nino: A Film About Nino Rota,” a documentary exploring the life and legacy of the Oscar-winning Italian composer, ahead of its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival, where it will screen in the Official…
body: Rota composed the music for Francis Ford Coppola’s “The Godfather” and “The Godfather Part II,” for which he won an Academy Award. “Nino: A Film About Nino Rota” is produced by Be Water Film (Mattia Guerra), Sugar Play (Filippo Sugar, Elisabetta Biganzoli), Adler Entertainment (Marco Colombo), I Diavoli, Marco Morabito and Fasano in collaboration with Rai Documentari, and with the support of MIC-DGCA Fondo per lo sviluppo degli investimenti nel cinema e nell’audiovisivo, Apulia Film Fund, Apulia Film Commission and Regione Puglia.
Be Water Film and Adler Entertainment will co-release the film in Italy.

articles.title: Memo to Ridley Scott: no one needs more Alien: Covenant movies – get the franchise back to stalk’n’slash
articles.summary: News that Scott is working on a follow-up to his maligned 2017 film leaves me worried the franchise has run out of shocks. If any science-fiction saga looked beyond recovery, it was the Alien franchise.
body: And then in 2024, we got Fede Álvarez’s Alien: Romulus, in which actual xenomorphs chase actual human beings down actual corridors for the clearly defined purposes of either killing them or putting smaller xenomorphs inside them. Better still, a year later we got Noah Hawley’s Alien: Earth, which reminded us that giant, murderous space insects are in fact less awful than tech trillionaires.

It’s not the first time Scott has talked up sequels to Covenant. During the publicity run for the film, he said a follow-up was already being written and that he would start shooting within 14 months. He also suggested he could make as many as six more Alien prequels, with the series eventually leading up to the original Alien. Eight years and no prequels later, Scott announced that he had “done enough” with the franchise and merely hoped it would continue without him. Now he appears to have reverted to an earlier mode.

articles.title: Online Sleuthing Is Out of Control, and the Vitriol Against Patrick Clancy Proves It
articles.summary: The trial of Lindsay Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse who admitted to strangling her three young children before attempting suicide in January 2023, has become the latest true crime sensation largely due to social media.
body: “He was having an affair, he plotted, drugged her, made her crazy, killed their kids. Tried to kill her. When she didn’t die, he convinced her he killed them. Framed her. Sent her to prison,” one Instagram user wrote in a widely shared post.

In a TikTok video posted on Aug. 17, Lisa Rinna, the former star of “The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills,” said, “All right, he did it. Patrick did it. Patrick’s the one who did it. Not Lindsay. Patrick did it. Because, you know, I also heard that women typically don’t strangle.”
But the Lindsay Clancy case is not a cold case. There is no mystery to be solved. Lindsay did it.

“The ONLY way I would consider marrying a man whose ex-wife supposedly murdered their 3 children and is now on trial for it….. is if I was already with him before it happened,” reads one Facebook comment.

articles.title: Not Your Daddy’s Films Expands With Film Independent as Fiscal Sponsor (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Not Your Daddy’s Films, a social impact organization focused on educating and elevating women and nonbinary filmmakers, is now fiscally sponsored by Film Independent, the non-profit independent media arts organization.
body: NYDF began as a bimonthly screening for 25 people, and has since grown into a thriving “Daddy community” with events drawing more than 300 attendees. Over the last four years, the organization has hosted screenings, workshops, panels and parties spotlighting women and nonbinary filmmakers, and partnered with industry institutions including the American Cinematheque, Alliance of Women Directors, SXSW, Women In Film (WIF) and The Black List.

NYDF will host its next event, a fourth anniversary party, on Friday at the Aster in Hollywood. Six up-and-coming filmmakers will showcase their work to the crowd of industry insiders before participating in a Q&A.

articles.title: The Whisper Man review – Robert De Niro sleepwalks through silly Netflix potboiler
articles.summary: A father and son must team up to find a serial killer in a cheaply made and increasingly uninteresting thriller. It’s not as if Robert De Niro ’s choices have improved all that much since the nadir of the mid-2000s (last year did see him crop up in a Scott Eastwood-led actioner and The Alto Knights…
body: It’s a familiar pile of B-movie schlock – serial killers, missing children, bumps in the night, more imaginary friends – and there is some initial junky fun to be had as we wonder just where it all might be headed. I was hoping for a destination a little more deranged or vaguely surprising, the film making a silent promise that we’re hurtling toward somewhere wildly unexpected before dumping us in a ditch instead.

Like Ashcroft, De Niro is on full checked-out autopilot mode, quietly mumbling perfunctory dialogue while seemingly focused on what he’ll be having for dinner, and Scott feels uncomfortably miscast, his other hard-drinking, fiction-writing genre turn of the year proving to be considerably more effective. An actor traditionally associated with comedy, he often falls into the Steve Carell trap of confusing sitcom histrionics with dramatic hysteria and so his pain and anger at the disappearance of his son never really registers (it would also require some miraculous heavy lifting to sell some of his character’s bafflingly dumb decisions).

articles.title: What we know after the big Grand Theft Auto 6 preview
articles.summary: The official look at the blockbuster video game leaves fans and critics impressed.
body: After more than 18 months since the last official glimpse of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar has shown fans a 26-minute preview of the upcoming blockbuster video game.
Its "extended look" debuted on Netflix, six hours before going live on YouTube, and was the first chance players have had to see detailed footage of the title in action.
The montage, with no commentary or explanatory captions, showed off improved graphics, detailed environments and a selection of car-chases and shoot-outs from the sequel.
The broadcast followed a week of unauthorised gameplay leaks, which the developer said it had been "heartbreaking" to see shared online.
points: The official look at the blockbuster video game leaves fans and critics impressed.

articles.title: Pierce Thiot, Creative Executive at Maximum Effort, Dies at 40
articles.summary: He worked on some of the biggest and most culturally relevant brand campaigns in recent memory for the studio and marketing agency founded by Ryan Reynolds and George Dewey.
body: Pierce Thiot, who as the head of creative for brand and entertainment at the film, television and marketing company Maximum Effort helped launch some of the most culturally relevant brand campaigns in recent memory, has died. He was 40.
Thiot died Tuesday at his home in Orem, Utah, from a pulmonary embolism, the company told The Hollywood Reporter.

At Maximum Effort, Thiot worked on some of the biggest stages in advertising and marketing, including a Super Bowl campaign featuring 50 Cent for DoorDash, a multibrand Oscars effort and original campaigns for L’Oréal Paris, Lancôme and TJ Maxx that served as extensions of the blockbuster film The Devil Wears Prada 2.

The company, and Thiot’s work, reflected the changing dynamics of marketing and advertising, with brands seeking to create work that was entertaining in its own right, and able to stand out from more traditional commercial campaigns.
